title: Flight-deck state becomes unsafe when aircraft state, automation mode, crew coordination, and training surfaces diverge
summary: Candidate pattern: cockpit/flight-deck accidents become more legible when actual aircraft state, displayed/interpreted state, automation mode, crew coordination, and training/procedure surfaces are factored separately. United 232 is included as a positive control so the pattern does not become pilot-error shorthand.

status_history.note: Created with four accident records, one positive control, and three infrastructure rails; no maturity claims allowed.

place.scope: commercial aviation flight-deck state and human-factors correction surfaces

subjects.name: flight-deck state divergence and CRM correction surface

claims.claim: The promoted rev0027 aviation records support a candidate pattern in which actual aircraft state, displayed/interpreted state, automation or warning mode, crew coordination, and training/procedure surfaces diverge enough that danger is not converted into timely safe action.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_refs.support_type: air-data/state legibility and man-machine interaction case

claims.claim: United 232 is a positive control showing that flight-deck coordination and CRM can be a resilience surface under catastrophic state degradation; therefore MKH-PAT-0022 must not mature as a “pilot error” or “crew failure” pattern.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_refs.support_type: CRM-positive control under catastrophic hydraulic loss

claims.claim: FAA Lessons Learned, FAA CRM guidance, and BEA/Annex 13 safety-investigation context are correction rails for this pattern, but none prove correction infusion, training effectiveness, or recommendation closure without child records.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: MKH-PAT-0022 remains candidate-only because it still needs additional positive controls, negative controls, non-aviation analogues, recommendation-closure records, and cases where automation/training successfully prevented harm.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_refs.support_type: red-team controls and maturity gate encoded in pattern record

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official landing-page / lessons-learned / legal-context extraction plus positive control
limitations: No full report extractions for all cases yet.
No recommendation-closure or training-effectiveness denominator yet.
No non-aviation human-factors analogue records in pattern support yet.

positive_controls_needed: Add Qantas 32, British Airways 009, or other source-backed cases where CRM, cross-checking, automation understanding, or procedural discipline helped convert abnormal state into survival.
Add near-miss/confidential-report examples where state divergence was caught before harm.
negative_controls_needed: Add a commercial-aviation accident where flight-deck coordination/state divergence was present but not causal, to prevent hindsight overfit.
Add a primarily structural/mechanical accident where crew response was competent and non-explanatory.
counterexamples_to_seek: Cases where increased automation reduced state divergence and prevented error.
Cases where CRM training was present and robust but physical-system damage exceeded survivable control envelope.
Cases where legal blame findings diverge from safety-investigation causal grain.
rollback_triggers: A second-pass full-report review materially weakens or reclassifies one of the support records.
The pattern is shown to conflate automation mode, crew communication, fatigue, and training into too broad a label.
Positive-control cases show the axis should be split into state-legibility, CRM, and training-infusion patterns.
The pattern is upgraded only after controls and not by record count alone.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: At least two positive controls, at least one negative control, at least one near-miss/prevention control, and a recommendation/training-infusion child record per major support family.

handling_notes: Aviation records must preserve the dignity of passengers, crew, families, responders, and survivors.
Do not flatten human-factors findings into pilot blame; separate physical system state, displayed state, automation mode, training, procedures, supervision, fatigue, and investigation/legal status.
This is historical/evidentiary infrastructure, not operational flight-safety guidance or legal advice.

unknowns: No full-report second-pass extraction for every case yet.
No recommendation-closure ledger for CRM, automation training, or FOQA/rulemaking changes yet.
AF447 legal-status developments are not encoded as causal safety findings.
next_actions: Add positive-control cases such as Qantas 32 and BA 009.
Add negative-control aviation accidents where crew coordination is not causal.
Create a recommendation-closure/training-infusion ledger for CRM, stall training, automation mode, and monitoring changes.
